d0cf010 fix: cost summary parsing now matches only actual cost summaries [90m(26/01/2026)[0m
  The regex patterns were matching `## Summary` headings in design documents
  (inside prompts) instead of the cost summary table at the end of log files.
  
  Root cause: Log files contain multiple `## Summary` sections:
  - Design doc summaries: `## Summary\n\n**Size: M**...`
  - Cost summaries: `## Summary (Updated after X)\n\n| Phase | Duration |...`
  
  The old regex `/## Summary.*?\n/` matched the FIRST occurrence, which was
  usually design doc content. This caused:
  - Phase data to not accumulate (each phase only showed itself)
  - Summaries from phases 1-4 to be lost/overwritten
  
  Fix: Both parseCostSummary and removeSummarySection now use specific patterns:
  - Require `---\n\n` prefix (added by generateSummaryMarkdown)
  - Require `(Updated after [Phase])` in title (unique to cost summaries)
  
  Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

7737c8a feat: add --global-limit flag to stop workflow after first agent processes items [90m(24/01/2026)[0m
  Add new --global-limit option for yarn github-workflows-agent --all that stops
  the entire workflow after the first agent successfully processes items.
  
  How it works:
  - Detects when an agent outputs "Processing N item(s)"
  - Stops running subsequent agents in the workflow
  - Allows next cron run to pick up where it left off
  
  Use case: Process items one at a time across the pipeline rather than batching
  within each phase. If implement agent processes 1 item, pr-review waits until
  next execution rather than running in the same workflow.
  
  Example:
    yarn github-workflows-agent --all --global-limit
  
  This is useful for:
  - Rate limiting overall agent execution
  - Processing items more gradually
  - Avoiding long-running cron jobs

  Changes" status.

  1. Agent successfully makes changes
  2. yarn checks auto-fix commits them

  1. Check if there are commits on branch (git log defaultBranch..HEAD)
  2. If yes, skip commit/push but continue to update Review Status
  3. If no, fail with error as before
  
  This allows the flow to complete and update Review Status even when:
  - yarn checks auto-committed fixes
  - Changes were committed in a previous run
  - Agent committed changes during its work
  
  ## Changes
  
  - Added hasChanges variable to track uncommitted changes
  - In feedback mode with no uncommitted changes, check for existing commits
  - Skip commit/push steps if no new changes but have existing commits
  - Continue to post comment and update Review Status
  - Properly handles the case where work is done but already committed
